title: Sequence-site internal Hom and punctual representation of mapping systems
statement:
Fix $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], a prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $R$, a uniformizer $\varpi$ and $A_n=R/\varpi^n$ for $n\ge1$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $f:X\to Y$ be separated finite type between separated finite-type $k$-schemes [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties], with compactification $X\xrightarrow{j}\overline X\xrightarrow{p}Y$ [def-weil-compactifications-refinements]. For $W=X,Y,\overline X$ and $\tau=\mathrm{et},\mathrm{proet}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site, def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], let $\mathscr S_W^\tau$ be the category of strict systems of $(A_n)_W$-module sheaves with semilinear quotient transitions and componentwise morphisms [lem-pur-coefficient-system-derived-comparison]; use its ordinary unbounded derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], exact evaluations $e_n$ and, for $m\ge n\ge1$, derived quotient functors $T^W_{m,n}=-\otimes^L_{A_m}A_n$ [def-weil-derived-tensor]. Write $t^M_{m,n}:T^W_{m,n}M_m\to M_n$ for the scalar-extension adjunct of the actual transition. 
Let $W=X$ or $Y$, write $H_W^{\mathrm{sys}}(M,N)$ for derived internal Hom on the ringed sequence site [def-pur-derived-internal-hom], and use for normalized $M$ [def-coef-normalized-dvr-tower] (every $t_{m,n}$ invertible) and arbitrary $N$ the canonical identifications
$$e_nH_W^{\mathrm{sys}}(M,N)\cong R\mathcal Hom_{A_n}(M_n,N_n),$$
carrying system evaluation to ordinary tensor-Hom evaluation, of [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections]; they exist on both sites $\tau$. If $M,N\in D(\mathscr S_W^{\mathrm{proet}})$ are both normalized, the comparison from the fiberwise Hom system $\mathcal I_W(M,N)$ [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus] to $H_W^{\mathrm{sys}}(M,N)$, defined as the closed transpose of its system evaluation, is invertible; under these identifications it evaluates to the identity of $R\mathcal Hom_{A_n}(M_n,N_n)$.
Now let $M,N\in D(\mathscr S_W^{\mathrm{et}})$ be normalized with bounded constructible finite-Tor levels [def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility, def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude]. The tensor/evaluation-defined comparison along [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism]
$$\nu_W^*H_{W,\mathrm{et}}^{\mathrm{sys}}(M,N)\longrightarrow H_{W,\mathrm{proet}}^{\mathrm{sys}}(\nu_W^*M,\nu_W^*N)$$
is invertible. For $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$ and $a_W:W\to s$, the etale coefficient system
$$\widehat{\mathcal H}_W(M,N)=Ra_{W,*,\bullet}^{\mathrm{et}}H_{W,\mathrm{et}}^{\mathrm{sys}}(M,N)$$
represents $P\mapsto\operatorname{Hom}(a_W^*P\otimes^LM,N)$ on $D(\mathscr S_s^{\mathrm{et}})$ (for this representability alone no finiteness of $M,N$ is needed). Its underlying abelian tower identifies canonically with $\mathcal H_W(\nu_W^*M,\nu_W^*N)$, the pro-etale mapping system obtained by total termwise derived global sections of $\mathcal I_W(\nu_W^*M,\nu_W^*N)$. This comparison uses the site-comparison unit and derived pushforward composition, preserves evaluation and transposition, and imposes no common bound on the levels.

proof.text: Apply the semilinear derived-sections calculus to the coefficient ring sequence on each chosen site. It supplies the canonical fiber identification for normalized $M$ and arbitrary $N$, including its evaluation normalization. For normalized pro-etale $M,N$, transpose the actual system evaluation $\mathcal I_W(M,N)\otimes^LM\to N$ using closedness on the sequence ringed site. The evaluated transpose is the transpose of ordinary evaluation, hence the identity of $R\mathcal Hom_{A_n}(M_n,N_n)$. Every evaluation of this comparison is therefore invertible, so joint conservativity makes the system comparison invertible. This uses existence of the evaluation map in the fiberwise-system lemma, rather than lifting an arbitrary family of maps.

source.place: Second paragraph, mapping-system comparison: assembly step 1

proof.text:
For etale normalized $M,N$ as in the statement, take the canonical ringed-topos pullback-Hom comparison on the sequence sites: its transpose is inverse-image of system evaluation after the tensor pullback comparison. Exact inverse image commutes with coefficient extension and hence preserves normalization. Evaluating this actual map and using the normalized Hom identifications gives the finite-level evaluation-defined comparison $
u_W^*R\mathcal Hom_{A_n}(M_n,N_n)	o R\mathcal Hom_{A_n}(
u_W^*M_n,
u_W^*N_n)$. The finite constructible comparison theorem applies: $W$ is finite type over $\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, $M_n$ is bounded constructible finite-Tor, and $N_n$ is bounded constructible. All evaluated maps are invertible, so the system comparison is invertible. No common interval is used.

source.place: Second paragraph, mapping-system comparison: assembly step 2

proof.text: Put $J=H_{W,\mathrm{et}}^{\mathrm{sys}}(M,N)$. Apply system inverse-image/direct-image adjunction to the structure morphism, and then the closed tensor-Hom adjunction on its source sequence ringed site. For every $P\in D(\mathscr S_s^{\mathrm{et}})$ this gives natural bijections $\operatorname{Hom}(P,Ra_{W,*,\bullet}^{\mathrm{et}}J)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(a_W^*P,J)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(a_W^*P\otimes^LM,N)$. The forward map is explicitly $h\mapsto\mathrm{ev}\circ(\varepsilon_J\otimes1_M)\circ(a_W^*h\otimes1_M)$, with $\varepsilon$ the structure-morphism counit. The inverse first curries and then takes the structure-morphism adjunct. The two adjunction identities prove they are inverse. This proves representability for arbitrary ambient $M,N$, independently of normalization and finiteness.

source.place: Second paragraph, mapping-system comparison: assembly step 3

proof.text:
Return to the finite-Tor constructible inputs. Form the actual system unit $J	o R
u_{W,*, ullet}
u_W^*J$. Its evaluation is the ordinary site-comparison unit at $J_n=R\mathcal Hom_{A_n}(M_n,N_n)$. The finite constructible-Hom theorem makes $J_n$ bounded constructible finite-Tor, so $J_n$ and $
u_W^*J_n$ lie in $D^+$. A bounded-below injective resolution of $
u_W^*J_n$ is K-injective [lem-weil-pbc-dplus-injective-representative](2), so the unbounded $R
u_{W,*,n}$ and its unit agree at $J_n$ with the bounded-below direct image and unit of the site-comparison theorem; thus the bounded-below full-faithfulness theorem makes this level unit invertible. Joint conservativity of exact system evaluation proves that the system unit is invertible even if the lower bounds of $J_n$ vary with $n$. Combine it with step 2 and the inverse of step 1 on the pro-etale side to obtain a specified isomorphism $J\cong R
u_{W,*, ullet}\mathcal I_W(
u_W^*M,
u_W^*N)$.

source.place: Second paragraph, mapping-system comparison: assembly step 4

proof.text: On $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$, the absolute Galois group is trivial. The abelian stalk equivalence and its terminal-section identification therefore identify etale abelian sheaves with abelian groups by the actual global-sections functor. It is exact, since an equivalence preserves kernels and cokernels. Adding $A_n$ actions and the transition equations gives the same identification for semilinear coefficient systems; forgetting the actions gives their underlying abelian towers. The inverse equivalence acts on the abelian groups and every scalar endomorphism, so no finite-generation condition occurs. Exactness and the exact-functor localization theorem identify derived point sections with this termwise underlying-tower functor.

source.place: Second paragraph, mapping-system comparison: assembly step 5

proof.text:
Apply $Ra_{W,*, ullet}^{\mathrm{et}}$ to the isomorphism in step 4, then take the point sections of step 5. Derived pushforward composition on the sequence ringed topoi identifies the result with total derived termwise sections of $\mathcal I_W(
u_W^*M,
u_W^*N)$ on the pro-etale site: both composites are the terminal sections functor on the pro-etale sequence site. Use the canonical composition comparison, followed by the scalar-forgetting/sections comparison of the sequence global-sections lemma: termwise sections followed by forgetting scalars equals termwise scalar restriction $U_W$ followed by termwise sections, and since forgetting scalars and $U_W$ are exact they are their own derived functors, so two further composition comparisons identify the derived composites with $R\Gamma^{\operatorname{Tow}}\circ U_W$ as maps in $D(\operatorname{Tow}(\operatorname{Ab}))$, whose evaluations are the level identifications of that lemma. By the definition in the evaluation-calculus lemma this is $\mathcal H_W(
u_W^*M,
u_W^*N)$. All arrows have been constructed before evaluation. The pullback-Hom arrow preserves evaluation and transposes by its cited normalization; the unit and composition arrows are the adjunction words, and system evaluation commutes with these transposes by the semilinear calculus. Thus this is the stated evaluation-preserving comparison. The sole bounded-below argument was at each separate $J_n$ in step 4; the pushforwards and composition here are unbounded.
